subject: Aligning on POC goals & measurement — NimblePay
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@nimblepay.com>, Raj Patil <raj.patil@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning on POC goals & measurement — NimblePay

Hi Sara / Raj —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before we draft a mutual action plan: 

Call highlights (recap)
- Primary use case: real-time authorization assistance for in-app payments (rule-based & support tickets).
- Peak expected load: ~40–60 RPS during peak windows, mostly short prompts (~120 tokens).
- Latency sensitivity: 95th percentile < 200ms is a hard requirement for authorization; target 99th < 500ms for degraded paths.
- Cost sensitivity: target marginal cost < $0.0009 per token for inference by end of POC.
- Quality metric: intent/decision-match accuracy on a 10k sample (baseline ~88%) — you want ≥95% for rollout.

Suggested POC scope (high level)
- Duration: 3 weeks of active evaluation + 1 week buffer for integration fixes (kickoff week of Apr 5).
- Redwood deliverables: hosted trial endpoint, sample traffic replay harness, baseline performance report, cost projection by workload.
- NimblePay deliverables: sample traffic dump (anonymized), acceptance test set (1000 labelled examples), security questionnaire answers.

Success criteria (for sign-off)
- Latency: 95th pct < 200ms (production-sim load), median < 60ms.
- Throughput: sustain 50 RPS with p95 SLA using dedicated instance config.
- Cost: estimated cost/token ≤ $0.0009 (inference-only) at POC config.
- Quality: decision-match accuracy ≥ 95% on your labelled acceptance set; false-positive rate for declined-authorizations ≤ 2%.

Timeline & immediate next steps
1) Mar 5–7: NimblePay shares anonymized traffic + label set and legal gives nod for test data (we received the xlsx you attached — thanks).
2) Apr 6: Redwood provisions trial endpoint and runs baseline on your sample traffic.
3) Apr 9–14: Integration run & tuning (batching/quantization profiles).
4) Apr 16–19: Joint review and go/no-go decision.

Owners
- Redwood: Marcus Lin (sales lead), Ben Carter (eng lead for integration).
- NimblePay: Sara Gomez (product), Raj Patil (CTO), Legal contact (procurement/DSA).

Can you confirm the timeline above and that your legal team can share the redlines or a limited DSA by Apr 7? Once confirmed, I’ll populate a short mutual action plan and calendar invites.

Attachments: nimblepay_requirements.xlsx (you attached during call)

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@nimblepay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patil <raj.patil@nimblepay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, legal@nimblepay.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Aligning on POC goals & measurement — NimblePay

Thanks Marcus — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifying items before I confirm with legal: 

1) Can Redwood confirm how you measure cost/token in the report? Is that inclusive of request overhead, or only per-token compute?
2) For the quality metric, we want to include a secondary metric: latency-triggered fallbacks. If model latency exceeds 500ms, the fallback path should preserve user experience; we want outage-impact < 0.5% during the POC.
3) Traffic sample: we’ll upload an anonymized AES-encrypted zip to the Drive link by EOD Monday (Apr 5).

If legal can do a light DSA (data processing addendum) by Apr 7 we can start. Also cc’ing Raj — Raj, do you want engineering to be on the kickoff call Apr 6 or should we sync resulting test harness details offline?

—Sara
Sara Gomez
Product Manager, NimblePay
sara.gomez@nimblepay.com | +1 (617) 555-2219

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@nimblepay.com>, Raj Patil <raj.patil@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, legal@nimblepay.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Aligning on POC goals & measurement — NimblePay

Sara — great, thanks for the quick read. Short answers inline and a concrete POC measurement plan attached.

On cost/token measurement
- We’ll report two numbers: (A) inference-only cost per generated token (GPU compute + model execution) and (B) end-to-end cost per API call (includes request/transport overhead, caching savings amortized). The POC target you called out maps to (A).

On latency fallbacks and outage impact
- Agreed: we’ll add a POC test that injects artificial latency and measures the user-impact rate. Goal: fallback path triggered <0.5% of successful flows during peak traffic.

Concrete POC Measurement Plan (excerpt)
- Baseline run (Apr 6): replay anonymized traffic at scaled rates (1x, 2x expected peak) and capture latency percentiles, tokens per call, and per-token cost.
- Integration run (Apr 9–14): test with real auth flow; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained throughput, and end-to-end success rate on labelled set.
- Quality validation (Apr 12–15): run acceptance set to calculate decision-match accuracy and false-positive rate; run A/B sample with current rule-based handler for delta.
- Reporting (Apr 16): consolidated report with KPI table, cost projection at scale, recommended config (quantized variant vs full precision), and suggested rollout guardrails.

POC KPI table (target vs pass criteria)
- Median latency (p50): target 50–60ms; pass p50 < 80ms.
- Tail latency (p95): target < 200ms; pass p95 < 300ms.
- Throughput: sustain 50 RPS at p95 SLA; pass sustain 40 RPS with no queueing.
- Cost (inference-only): target ≤ $0.0009/token; pass ≤ $0.0012/token.
- Quality: decision-match ≥ 95%; pass ≥ 92% (with documented mitigations if between 92–95%).
- Fallback impact: triggered <0.5% during peak; pass <1.5% with rollback plan.

Attachments: rwi_poc_template.pdf (POC plan), traffic-sample-202703.zip (we’ll use for replay once you confirm upload).

Next actions
- Sara: confirm Drive upload and legal timing (by Apr 7).
- Raj: confirm whether an engineering rep should join the Apr 6 kickoff (we recommend yes so Ben can pair on the baseline run).
- Ben: I’ll loop you to schedule the technical kickoff and share the runbook.

If that all looks good, I’ll post a short mutual action plan doc and send calendar invites for Apr 6 (kickoff) and Apr 16 (review).

Thanks —
Marcus

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

- cost-saver (aggressive quantization, smaller batch)

I’ll prep the runbook and the baseline script by EOD Apr 5 and be on the kickoff on Apr 6. If Raj wants eng on the call, invite him.
